newsitem.title: USA: United States objects ASEAN waiver proposal.
newsitem.headline: United States objects ASEAN waiver proposal.

text.p: The United States Tuesday voiced objections over a proposal made by ASEAN countries to seek waivers from WTO obligations for trade measures included in multilateral environmental agreements (MEAs).

The U.S. undersecretary of Commerce for International Trade, Stuart Eizenstat, said that such an approach would be inappropiate because it would place the World Trade Organization on a higher order of law than MEAs.
Eizenstat argued that since both the WTO and MEAs express the collective will of the international community, neither is more important than the other.

"In that respect, our view is that these issues should be resolved on a case-by-case basis. This is the best way to deal with them," he said in a speech at a conference on the environmental impact of the North American Free Trade Agreement.
Eizenstat said that the United States will put forward its full views on the issue at a WTO ministerial meeting in Singapore in December.
